name: mednafen
why: A multi-system emulator that doubles as a window into many old console architectures and their quirks.

brief.what_it_is: Mednafen is a portable, command-line-driven multi-system emulator built on OpenGL and SDL. It runs game images for many old consoles and handlers, including Apple II, Atari Lynx, Neo Geo Pocket, WonderSwan, Game Boy, GBA, NES, SNES, Virtual Boy, PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16 CD, SuperGrafx, PC-FX, Game Gear, Genesis/Mega Drive, Master System, Saturn (64-bit builds only), and PlayStation. Input is a ROM or disc image and the output is emulated video and audio on screen. It can also write PNG screenshots and QuickTime movies with lossless codecs. Hotkeys and virtual inputs can be remapped to a keyboard, a joystick, or both.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit mission statement. It presents Mednafen as a portable, accuracy-minded emulator that covers many systems in one program, configured from the command line and config files.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says emulation runs in a threaded model on top of SDL and OpenGL, and that this threading is why a joystick is preferred over a keyboard for lower input latency. Save states and real-time rewinding are supported. Per-module and per-game override configuration files exist, as the 1.32.0 notes describe.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists a source tarball (mednafen-1.32.1.tar.xz) and Windows zip builds for win64 and win32, each with a SHA-256 hash. The 1.27.0 notes mention a Windows 98-compatible build that is not provided every release. The 1.27.1 notes say the configure script errors out when iconv is missing. The 1.27.0 notes say the library dependency on libsndfile was dropped in favour of libFLAC. The page does not show a first-run walkthrough or any BIOS requirements, and the brew formula notes contain no extra caveats.
brief.standout: Mednafen is a single emulator that bundles many systems, and it has a long tail of accuracy work recorded in its changelogs, such as SNES VRAM write blocking and Saturn SCSP timing fixes. Its per-game fixes are listed by title in each release, so it reads partly as a record of how specific commercial games misbehaved on real hardware.
brief.status: Maintained as of the homepage. The newest entry is version 1.32.1, dated April 5, 2024, and the page footer says copyright 2005-2024. No later release or news item appears on the homepage. I did not check the GitHub or source repository for recent commits, so this rests on the homepage alone.
brief.caveats: Saturn emulation is 64-bit only. The minimum Windows 98-compatible build targets i686 with MMX, and PS1 MDEC emulation needs SSE2. Keyboard input has more latency than a joystick because of the threaded design. The 1.32.0 notes say the Windows 2000 build was restored for people who enjoy airgaps, firewalls, and insecurities. ST-V support is described as experimental. Licensing is GPLv2. The homepage footer notes that Mednafen is not an official Nintendo product.
quotes: Mednafen is a portable, utilizing OpenGL and SDL, argument(command-line)-driven multi-system emulator.
Mednafen is distributed under the terms of the GNU GPLv2.

Due to the threaded model of emulation used in Mednafen, and limitations of SDL, a joystick is preferred over a keyboard to play games, as the joystick will have slightly less latency, although the latency differences may not be perceptible to most people.
